subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should the public web-tool egress boundary be for this request: a scoped `web_fetch` hostname allowlist, a broader managed-proxy policy, or a cross-tool search/fetch/browser policy?
rationale: The requested config would be an operator-trusted exfiltration boundary, and current related PRs make different security/product choices that automation should not choose.

options.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping denylist, search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make managed proxy the boundary
options.body: Pause local web_fetch config work and route application-owned egress policy through the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Design a cross-tool policy
options.body: Require one design covering fetch, search, browser, providers, plugins, redirects, caches, and proxy behavior before implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Sponsor the narrow `web_fetch` hostname-allowlist path as an incremental first step, while keeping denylist, search, browser, and proxy coverage explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across SSRF, guarded fetch, web_fetch runtime, and docs surfaces involved in the boundary choice.
